newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down on technicals, cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down on technicals, cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended lower Tuesday, pressured by technical selling after Monday's reversal day and reports of softer physical prices, industry sources said.
April slipped 1.8 cents to close at $1.919 per million British thermal units. May settled 2.2 cent lower at $2.003. Most others ended off by one-half to 3.5 cents.

"We've come pretty far down and cash is holding the market up right now, but I think we'll move lower into the (March 24) April expiration," said one Midwest trader, noting suspected sell stops in April below $1.84 were not tested today.
But some said cool Northeast temperatures this week and next could keep the cash buoyant and limit the downside in paper near-term.
"Some people went into the month short, so there's been some buying in the cash, said one East Coast trader.

Technical traders said April's failure Monday to hold above $2 triggered some technical selling and liquidation today though they agreed recent ranges were intact. They noted good buying just below $1.90, with better April support still pegged at $1.78 and then at the $1.701 contract low. Important resistance was seen at $2.04, with further selling likely in the mid-teens and at $2.28.
Early withdrawal estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report ranged from 30 bcf to 85 bcf versus a 118 bcf draw a year ago.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices were steady to down slightly Tuesday in the high-$1.80s to $1.90 range. Midcon pipes were talked little changed in the $1.80 area. New York city gate swing gas was modestly lower at about $2.20.
The 12-month strip slid 1.1 cents to $2.115. NYMEX estimated volume figures were unavailable.
NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas did not trade Tuesday.

On the KCBT, April finished one cent lower at $1.69, while deferreds ended steady to down 2.3 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.8 cent to 22.9 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 187 lots changed hands, down from Monday's total of 547.
